transcript: in spring of 2025 on Broadway we're probably going to get the first revival of the Pulitzer winning musical Next To Normal the production that's currently playing on the west in is going to transfer to Broadway I hear and Next To Normal is a show that I feel very very very sentimental about it's one of the first musicals I discovered in high school and fell in love with and then just out of high school it's the first Broadway musical I ever saw completely I myself my family stayed in the hotel room I went and saw Next To Normal during its final week run in December of 2010and then on the way back to the hotel from Next To Normal I thought I'll stop at the Spider Man stage door and get Jennifer Damiato's autograph on my Next To Normal play Bill only for ambulances to rush down the street as I was waiting at the Spider Man stage door with then EMTs bursting inside and coming back moments later with Spider Man on a stretcher because it was the evening that that poor performer fell into the orchestra pit and I ran back into the hotel room and woke up my entire family yelling Spider Man's 😬 and I have pictures when I tell you I have Forrest gumped my way through so much of Broadway history but I digress I have a very very very soft spot for Next To Normal and if when next to normal comes back to Broadway hey that's another musical that composing team wrote he he he I will be one of the first people in line well theoretically who knows if I'll have money to go see that revival on Broadway but as somebody who has frankly dabbled with falling into a little psychosis and extreme mental illness in their life I do have to question the ending of Next To Normal as I get older and as I start to re evaluate the material as a proper adult as this is you know giant spoilers for those of you who have not seen Next To Normal but the musical basically ends with Diana not only walking out on her treatment but also walking out on her family on her husband and on her daughter who were her main mental support system and just wandering out into the world presumably to her parents house that's always told in a very very very uplifting way and as I get older I just start to wonder is there anything uplifting about this woman who very much needs extreme mental health care giving up on her doctor and just wandering off into the world and that's how she found light it's just the more I keep thinking about the ending of Next To Normal the more I keep thinking honey you don't need less treatment to beat this you might need a little bit more that all being said super excited for the Next To Normal revival who else was shaken to their core watching the Tony Awards that season when Diana threw the cutlery? who else thought that throw of the cutlery was just a revolution in the American musical theatre? because I know I did at the time
